analysis:
Examined all 12 units. The changes are: a new SelectedModelRecovery.swift (a pure value-type retry scheduler with backoff, pause, makeAllDue and nextDue, plus a Codable DaemonState.SelectedModelRecoveryEntry); additive StartupPreloader.Summary fields (failedInsufficientMemory, notAttempted) and isInsufficientMemoryLoad widened from private to internal; and the status CLI gaining pendingSelectionLines and recoveryLines.

No new network, crypto, attestation, authorization or at-rest data path is introduced. The scheduler holds only model IDs, timestamps, a check counter and a blocker string. Its backoff is bounded at 30s to 600s with a 15s pause, and the `attempt` task is held in memory and is not exercised by this code. The preloader changes only record extra summary data and do not alter admission or eviction. The load-gate and eviction-victim logic in `ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery` is not in the supplied evidence. That logic would determine whether a recovery can evict models, and whether it honors add-on holds (TB-012/T-059), the Autopilot lease, and the idle bound (`victimMinimumIdle`). Those behaviors are unverified here.

Status output is local-only, printed by the CLI from the owner-only daemon state. It includes model IDs and the `blocker` string. The `blocker` text's origin is not visible. If it can embed detailed memory values, that would be consistent with the existing owner-only-diagnostics posture. Nothing here reaches the coordinator or the public logs. The enabled_models diff strings are printed from the user's own config. I found no regression against TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-012, T-029 or T-041.

Open integration questions: how DaemonState persists and permissions the new fields (selectedModelRecovery, enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch), and whether the recovery eviction path respects holds and active requests.
